chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever allows himself to be taken captive without sustaining a heavy injury, he is not ransomed from the Public Treasury, but he is ransomed from his own wealth if his family wishes.

key_terms.اسْتَأْسَرَ: Allowed himself to be taken captive

ai.seo_question: Who pays the ransom for a prisoner of war who was not heavily injured during capture?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the financial responsibility for a prisoner of war who voluntarily submits without sustaining heavy injury, distinguishing between state treasury (bayt al-mal) coverage and personal family liability. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that negligence or voluntary capture shifts the burden of ransom from the public treasury to the individual's kin, emphasizing personal accountability in military conduct.
